checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are accurate and rigorous. It correctly identified that while the general silhouette (rectangular body, screen position) matches an iPod, the defining functional components (click wheel, UI) are missing or malformed. The Router did not skip any testable checkpoints unjustifiably. The 'untestable' verdicts for the back panel and hand-holding ergonomics are correct as those features are occluded or out of frame.

The 'texture_anomaly' on the screen (Severity 3) is also well-justified; the screen displays a hallucinated, blurry image rather than a coherent UI. The 'perspective_distortion' (Severity 2) on the edges is a valid observation of slight warping/softness typical of AI generation. The experts supported these findings: the classifier recognized the shape but the perceptual auditor noted blur, and the topology auditor confirmed a single mask (no floating parts), but the internal structure is flawed.
alignment_reasoning: The image fails to meet the core definition of the 'iPod' class due to the absence of the click wheel and proper UI. While the `fine_grained_classifier` predicted 'iPod' with high confidence (likely due to the strong prior of the rectangular black shape + screen), the visual evidence contradicts the taxonomy requirements for functional components. Only 3 out of 7 testable checkpoints passed (Body shape, Screen position, Casing material). The missing click wheel is a catastrophic alignment failure for this specific class.
artifact_reasoning: The image exhibits significant structural artifacts. The click wheel area is a 'smooth black void' (Severity 4), representing a failure to render complex mechanical interfaces. The screen content is nonsensical/hallucinated (Severity 3). Edges show slight warping (Severity 2). These are not minor aesthetic issues but fundamental failures in generating the object's defining features. The artifact score is low because the primary functional element is effectively melted/missing.
